absent: Full type definitions, sizes and alignments of raw spin, outer spin, read write and architecture lock objects.
Blocking acquisition waiting algorithm and fairness guarantees behind the double underscore lock helper.
Read write lock state machine and upgrade or downgrade rules on multiprocessor builds.
Bucket table sizing formula, hash distribution and lifetime management in the double underscore allocator.
Scoped guard expansion, lifetime and automatic release ordering.
Dependency map layout and acquire versus shared acquire checking rules.

Contended state detection used by is contended and need break queries.

findings.text: The raw layer provides a nonblocking acquisition helper that reports success and a release helper that relinquishes ownership. Acquisition consults the architecture primitive and on success performs a memory ordering facility before reporting. Release performs a memory ordering facility, delegates to architecture release, then marks the object released for static analysis.

Single processor architecture primitives appear in two build configurations. One maintains a small integer flag that is sampled then cleared on try with success tied to prior positivity, and is set to the unlocked encoding on release, with compiler ordering enforced around both. The other ignores its argument, enforces ordering only, and unconditionally reports success on try while doing nothing on release.

The public raw interface exposes blocking and nonblocking operations for plain, bottom half, interrupt, interrupt disable and interrupt save contexts. Each public name forwards to a corresponding underscored implementation, with the save variant adapting a caller flags word by address.

The outer spin wrapper mirrors the raw interface with plain, bottom half, interrupt and save forms for blocking acquisition, try acquisition, release, and state queries. Each wrapper operates on the embedded raw member obtained through a checked accessor and preserves conditional or unconditional acquisition annotations for analysis.

Nested acquisition forms accept either a subclass level or a second lock used for dependency ordering. In dependency tracking builds the subclass is forwarded and the second lock map is validated and forwarded, while in other builds the extra argument is ignored and the operation degrades to plain acquisition. Outer wrappers add annotation transfer from inner member to outer object around the raw call.

Interrupt save acquisition preserves caller interrupt state in a flags word. Depending on build, the wrapper either receives the saved state as a return value or passes the word by value to the underscored primitive, and nested save forms either forward subclass or ignore it and reuse the non nested save form.
Combined atomic decrement with lock acquisition helpers adapt a caller flags word by address when delegating to underscored implementations, with separate forms for outer spin and raw spin targets.

A bucket allocator macro supplies a static dependency key and a name derived from the table argument, forwards table, mask, sizing, scaling and allocation mode parameters to a double underscored helper, and returns that helper status to the caller.

Scoped guard support is exposed through constructor macros for raw, plain, read and write modes combined with plain, try, nested, interrupt, bottom half, save and initialization flavors. Each macro binds the generic guard attribute facility parameterized by its mode name.

On multiprocessor builds each single underscore raw operation aliases directly to a double underscore implementation with the same mode, covering blocking acquisition, try acquisition and release across plain, bottom half, interrupt and save contexts.

On single processor builds raw operations expand to small compositions that combine interrupt or bottom half masking with preemption control and static acquisition annotation, using exclusive annotation for spin and write and shared annotation for read, with symmetric unlock compositions restoring state.

Try acquisition reports success with a true or positive value and failure with false or zero, leaving the lock unchanged on failure. Multiprocessor try paths undo any preemption, interrupt or bottom half masking performed tentatively before reporting failure, so failed attempts have no masking side effect.

Single processor try operations always report success. Both the degenerate architecture primitive and the single processor API wrappers acquire masking and annotations then return success without any contention check.

Interrupt save forms require the caller flags word to be an unsigned long, validated at compile time. The saved value must be passed to the matching restore release, preserving the prior interrupt masking state across the critical section.

Outer spin operations never act on the wrapper directly but on its embedded raw member obtained via a dedicated accessor. Nested and save wrappers release the inner annotation and acquire the outer one around the raw call, keeping analysis ownership at wrapper granularity.

Break queries return false when the preemption model is not preemptible, without inspecting contention. Only in preemptible models do they forward to the underlying contended query for spin or read write locks.

Lock ownership assertion diverges by build. Multiprocessor builds raise a bug when the queried raw lock is not held, while single processor builds treat the check as a no operation that only references its argument. The single processor lock function classifier unconditionally reports false.

The realtime spin initializer accepts a lock reference, a name, a dependency key and a per cpu indicator but performs no action in the routed fragment, implying initialization is handled elsewhere or is a placeholder for that build.

Multiprocessor blocking acquisition first masks the context appropriate source, disables preemption, records dependency acquisition, then contends by attempting nonblocking acquisition before falling back to blocking wait. Save forms additionally preserve interrupt state for later restore, bottom half forms use a lock offset when disabling bottom halves.

Multiprocessor release first records dependency release, then performs raw unlock, then restores prior execution state in reverse order of acquisition. Plain release reenables preemption, interrupt forms restore interrupt masking before reenabling preemption, and bottom half forms reenable bottom halves with the same offset used on entry.

Single processor acquisition provides no spinning or atomic exclusion beyond masking. Plain forms only disable preemption with annotation, bottom half forms disable bottom halves, interrupt forms disable or save interrupts plus preemption, and unlock forms restore in reverse. Subclass arguments are accepted but ignored.

Read acquisition uses shared ownership annotation while spin and write acquisition use exclusive annotation, on both single and multiprocessor compositions. Unlock paths use the matching shared or exclusive release, preserving read versus write distinction for analysis.

Fragments reveal partial object layouts. A raw spin object exposes an architecture state member and a dependency map member. An outer spin object embeds a raw member accessed by the checked accessor. Single processor architecture state holds a single byte flag. Allocation uses a static dependency key object alongside the table.

The single processor byte flag encodes unlocked as positive and locked as cleared. Try samples the prior value then clears, moving from unlocked to locked on success and reporting success only from unlocked. Release moves unconditionally to unlocked. The degenerate configuration has a single state that always reports success.

Multiprocessor try follows tentative masking then test. From unmasked it enters masked tentative state, attempts raw acquisition, on success remains masked and held with dependency recorded, on failure returns to unmasked and unheld with no dependency effect. Blocking acquisition loops the same test until held.

Public entry points for drivers and core code are the outer spin and raw families for blocking lock, try lock and unlock across plain, bottom half, interrupt and save contexts, plus state queries, break hints, combined atomic decrement with lock, bucket allocation and scoped guard constructors. Underscored and double underscored names are internal dispatch layers selected by build.

Single processor configurations provide no atomic mutual exclusion. The degenerate architecture primitive and the masking only API wrappers always succeed, so code relying on try failure for correctness will never observe contention and concurrent interrupt or preemption misuse can corrupt shared state.

Subclass and nest lock arguments are silently discarded in builds without dependency tracking and in some nested save fallbacks, and subclass is ignored on single processor paths. Callers cannot rely on ordering validation in those builds, and mismatched save with plain restore or mismatched context unlock would corrupt interrupt or bottom half state.

Raw acquisition and release pair architecture primitives with memory ordering helpers that must not be omitted. Skipping the ordering on success or on release can expose weakly ordered input output accesses to reordering across the critical section.

The single processor flag uses value one for unlocked and value zero for locked, with any positive sample treated as unlocked on try. Try success is reported as one or true and failure as zero or false. These encodings are relied upon by callers checking return status.

Interrupt save state is carried in an unsigned long flags word preserved across the critical section. Header identity macros guard multiprocessor, single processor and realtime spin interfaces against multiple inclusion.
